policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the word verbally, as a relative clause 'who should prophesy', which is the niphal participle of the qere הַנִּבְּאִים. The ketiv spelling הנביאים, with the yod, is the plural noun נְבִיאִים 'the prophets'; had the ASV followed it the phrase would name the men prophets rather than describe their service, as it does elsewhere in the verse ('set apart for the service ... certain of the sons of Asaph'). The wording therefore distinguishes the qere.
